response.sql: WITH side_counts AS (SELECT o.dealedge AS side, COUNT(*) AS cnt FROM riskandmargin rm JOIN orders o ON rm.ordervault = o.recordvault WHERE o.dealedge IS NOT NULL GROUP BY o.dealedge), avg_side AS (SELECT AVG(cnt) AS avg_cnt FROM side_counts), above AS (SELECT sc.cnt, sc.cnt - a.avg_cnt AS excess FROM side_counts sc CROSS JOIN avg_side a WHERE sc.cnt > a.avg_cnt) SELECT SUM(cnt) AS total_count, AVG(excess) AS avg_excess FROM above;

assumptions.assumption: The inner join drops risk/margin records with no matching order. Sides are the distinct non-NULL dealedge values that have at least one matched record, and the average is taken over those sides only.
If no side's count exceeds the average (for example, two sides with equal counts), the query returns one row with NULL values.

alternatives.interpretation: Average across both fixed order sides, Buy and Sell, including a side with zero matched records as a count of 0.
alternatives.sql: WITH sides(side) AS (VALUES ('Buy'), ('Sell')), side_counts AS (SELECT s.side, COUNT(rm.riskandmarginpivot) AS cnt FROM sides s LEFT JOIN orders o ON o.dealedge = s.side LEFT JOIN riskandmargin rm ON rm.ordervault = o.recordvault GROUP BY s.side), avg_side AS (SELECT AVG(cnt) AS avg_cnt FROM side_counts), above AS (SELECT sc.cnt, sc.cnt - a.avg_cnt AS excess FROM side_counts sc CROSS JOIN avg_side a WHERE sc.cnt > a.avg_cnt) SELECT SUM(cnt) AS total_count, AVG(excess) AS avg_excess FROM above;
